pixel_observations.visible_description: Axial non-contrast CT image of the head showing the skull base and calvarium. A bright hyperdense focus with radial streak artifact is visible near the midline anteriorly. The calvarium appears intact in the displayed slice. Label 'A' below the image and 'R' marker on left side of image.

attribution_evidence.quote: CTA of the head demonstrated a metallic foreign body lodged at the right internal carotid artery (ICA) terminus with an intact calvarium and no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or trauma (Figure 1(A)).

pixel_observations.visible_description: Axial CT angiography image of the head showing contrast opacified intracranial vessels. A bright metallic artifact with streaking is present centrally. Vascular structures are visible in the brain. Label 'B' below the image.

attribution_evidence.quote: Vessel imaging showed occlusion of the M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) with distal reconstitution of the MCA vasculature, although this was obscured by streak artifact from the metal fragment (Figure 1(B)).

pixel_observations.visible_description: Sagittal or oblique CTA image of the neck showing the cervical spine and contrast opacified carotid artery. The vessel appears narrowed in the cervical region. Bony cervical vertebrae are visible. Label 'C' below the image.

attribution_evidence.quote: Additionally a smooth stenosis of the right ICA from the level of C3 to the petrous portion of the ICA was also appreciated concerning for possible vasospasm secondary to the travel of embolic metal fragment (Figure 1(C)).

pixel_observations.visible_description: CT perfusion RAPID map display with multiple small axial slices arranged in a grid. Color overlays include magenta and green regions. Text at bottom reads 'RAPID', 'CBF <30% 40 ml', 'Mismatch volume: 102 ml', 'Mismatch ratio: 3.5', 'Tmax>6s 142 ml'. Labels 'CBF', 'Tmax' at top of the panel. Label 'D' below the image.

attribution_evidence.quote: CT perfusion of the brain was subsequently obtained and demonstrated a large 102 ml mismatch between penumbra and core infarct (Figure 1(D)).
